700680.t: Originally the neuter accusative plural of ἄλλος (állos, “another, different”) with shifted accent in an adverbial sense, from Proto-Indo-European *h₂élyos (“other”).

700656.t: From ἀληθής (alēthḗs, “true”) + -ια (-iă, abstract noun suffix). Synchronically analyzable as ἀληθής (alēthḗs) + -εια (-eia).

700697.t: From Proto-Hellenic *ál͏̌l͏̌os, from Proto-Indo-European *h₂élyos. Cognates include Latin alius, Old Irish aile, Old Armenian այլ (ayl), Old English elles (English else).

700610.t: From Proto-Indo-European *h₂eḱrós (“sharp”). Cognates include Old Church Slavonic остръ (ostrŭ), Latin ācer, Old Armenian ասեղն (asełn, “needle”) and Old English ēagor (English eagre).

700645.t: From ἀλέκτωρ (ăléktōr, “cock, rooster”) + -υών (-uṓn, an obscure suffix also appearing in ἀλκυών (alkuṓn, “kingfisher”)).

700642.t: Disputed. Perhaps from Proto-Indo-European *h₂leg- (“to care”), and related to ἀλέγω (alégō, “to take care”).

700608.t: Neuter of ἄκρος (ắkros, “topmost, outmost, inmost; highest”).

700658.t: From ἀ- (a-, “un-”) + *λῆθος (*lêthos, “*concealment”) + -ής (-ḗs). *λῆθος (*lêthos) is the neuter σ-stem abstract noun to the root of λανθάνω (lanthánō, “I am hidden”), the existence of which is warranted by its Doric variant λᾶθος (lâthos).

700653.t: From Proto-Indo-European *h₂léh₁wr̥. Cognate with Old Armenian ալեւր (alewr).

700615.t: From an uncertain source apparently shared with Sanskrit अक्तु (aktú, “beam, ray”), perhaps: * Proto-Indo-European *h₂ekt- (“beam”), from an unidentified root; * Proto-Indo-European *h₂eḱ- (“sharp point”), which would exclude the Sanskrit; *…

700644.t: From Proto-Indo-European *h₂leybʰ-. Cognate with Latin lībō.

700605.t: The first element is ἄκρος (ắkros, “topmost; outermost”). The second element is uncertain; it was traditionally thought to be βύω (bŭ́ō, “to stuff; to plug”), but this is almost certainly incorrect.

700689.t: From phrases such as ἄλλος ἄλλον (ắllos ắllon), ἄλλοι ἄλλους (ắlloi ắllous, “one another”), with loss of λ either by dissimilation or by the lengthening of α, as well as restoration of the second initial vowel ή (ḗ) (< *h₂élyos (“other”)).

700629.t: It matches Thracian Ἀλαζών (Alazṓn) exactly, perhaps an appellative, or it may be a cultural loanword from Akkadian 𒀀𒇻𒍣𒉡 aluzinnu, 'boastful, clownish fraud, most times pretending or claiming to possess medical skills or knowledge.' From Sumerian 𒀩𒍪…

700667.t: From ἁλής (hālḗs, “thronged, crowded”) + -ίζω (-ízō), from Proto-Indo-European *wel- (“to push, press”).

700665.t: From ἅλς (háls, “salt, sea”) + -εύς (-eús, suffix for person concerned).

700609.t: From ἄκρος (ắkros, “at the edge; extreme, outermost”) + πόλις (pólĭs, “city; the Athenian citadel”).

700622.t: Probably cognate with ἄκρος (ắkros), but Beekes considers this uncertain.

700696.t: From Proto-Hellenic *həl͏̌l͏̌omai, from Proto-Indo-European *sl̥yétor, from the root *sel-. Cognate with Latin saliō (“to jump”) and Sanskrit सरति (sárati, “to run”).

700638.t: From ἄλγος (ắlgos, “pain of the body or mind”) + -έω (-éō, verbal suffix).

700683.t: From ἀλλαγή (allagḗ, “change”) + -σσω (-ssō), though Beekes considers ἀλλάσσω (ăllắssō) to be original and ἀλλαγή (allagḗ) a derivative. Either way, ultimately from ἄλλος (állos, “other”).

700688.t: Borrowed from Biblical Hebrew הַלְּלוּיָהּ (halləlūyɔh, “praise the Lord”).

700666.t: Denominal verb of ἁλιεύς (halieús, “fisher”); also analyzable as ἅλς (háls, “saltwater, seawater”) + -εύω (-eúō).

700672.t: Ritual term of unknown origin. Fur.: 298 compares λιγνύς (lignús, “smoke, soot”), which supposes a prothetic vowel and interchange σ/zero before velar (highly uncertain).
